note: Assumptions-and-gaps register for the D2 I-95 pedestrian bridge. Each entry is a small engineering gap, placeholder, assumption or judgment that lives in one place here instead of in decision prose, notebook pending lists, journal text or tracker rows. Hand-edited and committed; the design atlas (design_atlas/build.py) shows the entries on their related nodes and tools/project_coherence.py validates them. An entry records the magnitude the judgment rests on, not the engineering values the journal owns. 'basis' maps register source ids to the SHA-256 the entry was judged against; the generator marks an entry stale when the source register now adopts a different revision of any basis source. Nothing here is generated: the atlas 'Draft assumption' form only produces JSON to paste into 'entries'. Entry shape: {id: A-###, kind: assumption|gap|placeholder|judgment, statement, where, nodes: [atlas node ids], magnitude: {value, unit, sized_by}, disposition: {status: accepted-negligible|pending|closed, decision: D-0xx, on: YYYY-MM-DD}, owner, coherence_items: [COH-###], basis: {source id: sha256}, references: [repository paths]}.

entries.statement: The bearing dead load entered in the three FBMP fixed-run exports is the pre-T014 journal value (92.07 kip per bearing). The post-T014 journal haunch volumes raise End Bent 1 to 92.473 kip (+0.40 kip) and lower End Bent 2 by 0.38 kip, with a net +0.03 kip at the pier.
entries.where: FBMP nodal loads at end-bent nodes 15 and 34 and the pier bearing rows; journal FBMPEndBent and FBMPPier entry tables.

magnitude.sized_by: Export DC FZ 92.07 kip against the T018-recalculated journal FBMPEndBent value 92.473 kip (0.4% of the bearing dead load).

entries.statement: The D-059 pier cheek walls (48 x 48 x 12 in at each cap end, 4 ft above the cap top) add exposed area outside the 230-in pier face that is not in the pier FBMP model: about +1.92 kip transverse and +0.48 kip longitudinal direct wind at Strength III.
entries.where: Pier FBMP direct-wind nodal loads (node 49 transverse, nodes 117/83 longitudinal); journal FenceWind direct-pier terms; CAD model pier cheek walls.

magnitude.sized_by: 2 x 16 ft2 transverse (and 2 x 4 ft2 longitudinal) cheek-wall area at p_sub_III = 0.060 ksf; about 3% of the 56.5 kip total transverse wind on the pier.

entries.statement: The end-bent bearing eccentricity and longitudinal-wind moments about the transverse axis (MX = 0 in both end-bent exports; 23.0 kip-ft DC, 7.2 kip-ft PL and up to 31.8 kip-ft wind per bearing in the journal entry table) are carried by the backwall tie-back straps of the backwall design (D-057), not by the pile row.
entries.where: End-bent FBMP nodal loads at nodes 15 and 34 (y = 0 on the centered pile line); journal FBMPEndBent MX rows; backwall report strap loads.

magnitude.sized_by: Largest per-bearing MX in the journal FBMPEndBent table (WS1, bearing eccentricity plus longitudinal-wind arm); DC 23.017 and PL 7.246 kip-ft from the 3-in bearing eccentricity.

entries.statement: Backwall self-weight (77.77 ft3, 11.67 kip per end bent) and the landing weights (111.5 / 88.6 ft3, 16.7 / 13.3 kip, 50% bearing on the backwalls per D-016) are not in the end-bent FBMP models; the strap pile-head equilibrium force of the backwall report is likewise unmodeled.
entries.where: End-bent FBMP nodal loads; end-bent pile design cases that read those exports.

magnitude.sized_by: Backwall volume 77.770 ft3 from the D-057 case x 0.150 kcf, per end bent; landings 16.7 / 13.3 kip with half on the backwalls.

entries.statement: End-bent direct wind is not modeled; the journal entry table notes it needs end-bent geometry. A fully exposed cap front and backwall face (about 60 + 78 ft2) would give about 8 kip longitudinal at Strength III, but the closure slab and deck end cover most of that strip and the MSE returns shield the ends.
entries.where: End-bent FBMP nodal loads; journal FBMPEndBent and FenceWind modules.

magnitude.sized_by: Upper bound: fully exposed cap front plus backwall face (about 138 ft2) at p_sub_III = 0.060 ksf; actual exposure is much smaller.

entries.statement: The 3.00 kip DC loads at end-bent nodes 7 and 4 are placeholders for unmodeled concrete, the only such entries in the end-bent exports; one of them sits on the head of pile 4.
entries.where: End-bent FBMP nodal loads (nodes 7 and 4); backwall design basis (BACKWALL_DESIGN.md).

magnitude.sized_by: Placeholder value as entered; compare with the unmodeled backwall gravity of A-004 (11.67 kip per end bent).

entries.statement: The 3.00 kip DC loads at pier nodes 5 and 44 are placeholders that now stand for the D-059 pier cheek walls, 2.34 kip each (31.26 ft3 total), within the placeholder value.
entries.where: Pier FBMP nodal loads (nodes 5 and 44); CAD model pier cheek walls.

magnitude.sized_by: Cheek-wall weight from the D-059 adoption summary (15.63 ft3 x 0.150 kcf each) against the 3.00 kip placeholder.

entries.statement: The End Bent 2 export carries the End Bent 1 bearing loads (92.07 / 28.98 kip) instead of the journal's span-2 tributary values (89.967 / 28.323 kip), which is 2.3% conservative.
entries.where: End Bent 2 FBMP nodal loads; End Bent 2 cap and pile cases that read the export.

magnitude.sized_by: Export bearing DC 92.07 kip against the journal span-2 tributary 89.967 kip.

entries.statement: The pier pipe pile is checked with ASTM A252 Grade 3 (Fy = 45 ksi) in the pile design. The 19 October FBMP pier model used 60 ksi; the 21 October rerun (D-073) models the pile at 45 ksi, so the Fy reconciliation is closed by the registered export. The grade selection and the corrosion allowance remain design inputs (pile prerequisites corrosion, exposure).
entries.where: Pier pile design case and report; journal PileDesignPier, PileProperties and FoundationModeling modules; pier FBMP model pile material.

magnitude.sized_by: Difference between the FBMP pile material Fy (45 ksi since D-073; 60 ksi in the D-049 export) and the 45 ksi design grade (D-050, D-056).

entries.statement: The MSE exclusion side walls re-extracted from the D-055 model sit at the 24-in criterion within 0.0002 in, so two of four side-wall rows read SHORTFALL by their last digits (T016).
entries.where: Journal MSE Wall Exclusion module; CAD model MSE wall lines; MSE detail drawing.

magnitude.sized_by: Side-wall offset 114 in from the pile rows against the 24-in clear criterion, as recorded by the T016 re-extraction.

entries.statement: The 19 October pile design reports carry pending prerequisites: the downdrag source documentation, scour, the minimum tip elevation and the pile-to-cap connection (with pipe steel grade, corrosion allowance, drivability and environment classification).
entries.where: End Bent 1, End Bent 2 and Pier pile design reports and cases; journal pile design modules.

magnitude.sized_by: Not a load difference: unconfirmed inputs (15, 15 and 16 pending entries per report under D-054).

entries.statement: The pile-row wall loads of the pier FBMP model were entered from the former 114.737 kip pier wall (213 x 36 x 172.375 in). Under D-075 the wall is the CAD wall, 219 x 36 x 194.8625 in: 133.359 kip gross (112.1 kip net of the four pile bores), +18.6 kip (+16%) on the pier pile group, about +4.7 kip per pile. The export is unchanged pending the next FBMP rerun decision. Re-checked the same day against the D-076 CAD revision (pier wall steel and rings added; wall geometry unchanged).
entries.where: Pier FBMP nodal loads at the pile rows (pier wall self-weight split per the FBMP entry note); journal gravity sheet row 42 (W_wall) and the C004 information row; pier pile case demands.

magnitude.sized_by: CAD wall gross weight 889.06 ft3 x 0.150 kcf = 133.36 kip against the 114.74 kip entered (16%); about 2% of the factored pier pile group load of the D-073 export.

entries.statement: The pier pile case and the FBMP pier model use ground EL 26.05 ft; the journal (Terrain_elev) and the CAD model use terrain EL 25.5264 ft at the pier, 6.3 in lower. The D-075 pier wall free length to fixity (92.4 in) subtracts the 18.3 in of wall below the pile-case ground; with the CAD terrain it would be 98.4 in, which changes the ring moment by about 6% (5.40 to about 5.1 kip-in per ring) with every ring still in full contact (equivalent eccentricity about 1.1 in against the 5.19 in kern). Re-checked the same day against the D-076 CAD revision (wall geometry unchanged).
entries.where: Pier pile case EL_ground; FBMP pier soil top; journal BridgeGeometry_2Beam Terrain_elev; CAD pier wall bottom (GroundElevation - WallBurial); ring wall case pile_free_length_in.

magnitude.sized_by: EL 26.05 (pile case / FBMP) less EL 25.5264 (journal / CAD terrain) = 0.5236 ft; effect on the C017 ring moment about 6%, no status change.
